items.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: Count Basie was going, Lester Young

ctx.x: Is there let’s say a decade, a ten year span, where the music of that ten year span was really a favorite for you?

Yeah I think when Charlie Parker started and Dizzy Gillespie and Count Basie was going, Lester Young. Maybe the 30s and 40s, back. I don’t know, well then Miles came along. It’s all good, it keeps going, it gets going fast for me though with a lot of the real modern guys. But I guess I’m getting a little older. I love the rhythm music. I love the bebop. That was so new. And I don’t think — nobody that I’ve heard plays much better

than Charlie Parker. Oh but Louis Armstrong too, nobody plays better than him really, you hear the records he made, that guy. And then these new kids, what is it Roy Hargrove, he’s great too. There’s just all kinds of talent.
